title: Critical AI capability, active exploitation and control evidence now meet in one operating test
mainJudgement: The week’s evidence turns capability, exploitation, sanctions change and resilience into one practical test: can the firm see risk early, intervene quickly and reconstruct the decision?

committeeQuestion.question: For the risks we say are critical—agentic AI, exploited vulnerabilities, sanctions change and data failure—can management show the trigger, intervention authority, evidence of action and closure decision?
committeeQuestion.why: This week’s signals are different in form but identical in management demand: speed matters only when the firm can recognise the trigger, act within authority and preserve a decision trail that survives challenge.
committeeQuestion.evidence: Ask for one recent end-to-end example: the alert or evaluation, named owner, authority to intervene, control action, exception decision, recovery or remediation proof, and dated closure record.

judgement.observation: OpenAI says testing cannot rule out critical cyber capability in an upcoming model; CISA records active exploitation; an OFSI licence amendment changes a sanctions permission; and ICO action keeps data-control evidence live. Japan’s FSA keeps resilience in the same frame.
judgement.executiveJudgement: These signals are different in form but share a failure mode: risk is recognised, yet no one can show who may intervene, what control action was taken, whether an exception was accepted, or how the decision closed. Policies and dashboards do not answer that question.
judgement.implication: Choose genuinely critical scenarios and demand one reconstructable decision trail for each: trigger, owner, authority, action, evidence, recovery or remediation, and closure. Start with model evaluations, exploited assets, sanctions change and sensitive-data failure.
